"""Component p-82af68dd layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3392: prepositional phrases.

Plain terms: the component is mildly positive on a preposition itself ("in", "through", "via"),
and strongly negative on the words that open the phrase's object: the word right after the
preposition, most of all when it is a determiner or quantifier ("in THE", "for SOME", "at ALL"),
and the noun after "preposition + determiner" ("in the MAJORITY of"). The negative values are
largest for locative and temporal prepositions (in, for, from, at, on, within, during) and small
for of, to, as, like, since and than. Everywhere else it stays near zero.

The program looks back at most three tokens within the same clause and carries no state.
On the eval rows this rule explains about 18 percent of the variance (Pearson r 0.42). Most of
the rest depends on context it does not model.
"""

READS = ()

PREPOSITIONS = frozenset(
    "in at on for from with by to of into during among within between under over about "
    "after before through across against without per via upon toward towards near inside "
    "outside throughout along around behind beyond like as than since until despite amid "
    "above below beneath".split()
)

WEAK_PREPOSITIONS = frozenset("of to as like since than".split())

DETERMINERS = frozenset(
    "the a an this that these those some many all every each several various certain more "
    "most other any no such what which something anything both few much another either "
    "neither its his her their our my your one".split()
)

CLAUSE_BREAKS = frozenset(".;:!?\n,()")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    cur = strings[t].strip().lower()
    if cur in PREPOSITIONS:
        return carry, 0.4
    # Distance back to the nearest preposition in the same clause, at most three tokens.
    gap = None
    for g in range(1, 4):
        j = t - g
        if j < 0 or prefix.document_ids[j] != prefix.document_ids[t]:
            break
        if strings[j].strip().lower() in PREPOSITIONS:
            gap = g
            break
        if CLAUSE_BREAKS & set(strings[j]):
            break
    if gap is None:
        return carry, 0.0
    weak = strings[t - gap].strip().lower() in WEAK_PREPOSITIONS
    det_here = cur in DETERMINERS
    det_before = strings[t - 1].strip().lower() in DETERMINERS
    if gap == 1:
        # The word right after the preposition: strongest when it opens a noun phrase.
        if weak:
            value = -1.8 if det_here else -0.6
        else:
            value = -3.3 if det_here else -2.1
    elif gap == 2 and det_before:
        # The noun after "preposition + determiner".
        value = -1.6 if weak else -3.0
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Layer-15 MLP down_proj component 3393: a digit detector that cares where
in the line the number sits.

Digits push it negative, and most strongly the digits of a number that opens
a line (line numbers, list items, table cells): the first, second and third
digit there. The third digit of a year-like number (19xx, 20xx) is also strongly
negative, even mid-sentence. Other digits sit near zero, and the end-of-text
token is strongly negative. Ordinary words and punctuation are near zero.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")
END_OF_TEXT = "<|endoftext|>"
LINE_START_TOKENS = 5  # a number this close to its line's start counts as opening the line

# mean activation by (digits so far, opens the line?)
OPENING = {1: -3.0, 2: -5.0, 3: -6.0}
OPENING_LATER = -2.8  # fourth and later digits of a line-opening number
MID_LINE = {1: -0.5, 2: -0.5, 3: -1.5}
MID_LINE_LATER = -1.0
YEAR_THIRD_DIGIT = -5.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    ts, docs, i = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids, prefix.position
    tok = ts[i]
    if tok == END_OF_TEXT:
        return carry, -8.8
    if tok not in DIGITS:
        return carry, -0.1
    # the digits of this number so far
    s, j = "", i
    while j >= 0 and ts[j] in DIGITS and docs[j] == docs[i] and len(s) < 6:
        s = ts[j] + s
        j -= 1
    n = len(s)
    if n == 3 and s[:2] in ("19", "20"):
        return carry, YEAR_THIRD_DIGIT
    # how many tokens since the line began (stopping at a newline or document start)
    since, k = 0, i
    while k >= 0 and docs[k] == docs[i] and "\n" not in ts[k] and since <= LINE_START_TOKENS:
        since += 1
        k -= 1
    if since <= LINE_START_TOKENS:
        return carry, OPENING.get(n, OPENING_LATER)
    return carry, MID_LINE.get(n, MID_LINE_LATER)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3395 (component 3395 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj).

What it is: one hidden unit of layer 15's MLP, written into the residual stream
with a fixed weight. Most of the time it is near zero, and token identity
explains almost none of its variance. Its large values (either sign) are rare
and erratic, so this program captures only the parts that are regular:

  - Near the start of a document (positions counted from the last document
    boundary, as the model resets them) the unit is pushed negative when the
    token is not a word: strongly at position 1, weaker at positions 2-6.
    At position 1 it is only slightly negative for ordinary words.
  - The NUL control character ("\\x00") is strongly negative.
  - A hyphen that ends a line ("-\\n", a word broken across lines) is
    positive.
  - Everything else is 0.

Words are tokens whose text, without spaces, is letters only.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the token's index inside its document, or None at a row's first token
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry + 1
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().isalpha()
    value = 0.0
    if pos == 1:
        value = -1.3 if word else -4.0
    elif 2 <= pos <= 6 and not word:
        value = -0.9 if pos == 2 else -0.3
    if text == "\x00":
        value = -4.0
    if text == "-\n" and pos >= 2:
        value = 3.0
    return pos, value

"""Constant predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3396.

This component's activation has no simple description: it is a diffuse,
context-dependent direction in layer 15's MLP hidden space (mostly
neuron 3396, but spread over thousands of other neurons), with mean
about 0.02 and std about 0.29. Its token identity, token category,
position in the document and repetition explain almost none of its
variance (held-out R^2 under 0.3%). So the best simple prediction is the
mean value everywhere.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0195


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3397: a near-constant, context-free contribution.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's down projection. Its activation is
(hidden . V_c) * |U_c|. Its input direction is dominated by MLP hidden unit 3397 (about a
third of its variance) plus many small, diffuse hidden units. Measured on training text,
its activation is roughly symmetric around 0 with std about 0.32, and it is essentially
unpredictable from the text: a per-token lookup explains about 0.1% of variance on rows it
was not fit on, character classes add nothing, and position or repetition barely shift the
mean. It never passes the harvest's causal-importance threshold, and switching it off
barely changes the model's output.

What this program does: it predicts the component's mean activation (about 0.008) at every
position. That is the least-squares answer available from the text, and it leaves the
output almost exactly as switching the component off does. Nothing readable from the text
explains its variance.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.008


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The activation does not depend on the prefix in any way we could name.
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Early-document signal for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3398.

The component is silent on the first token of a text, then strongly negative
over the next few dozen tokens. Its size falls off with distance from the
start: about -12 on the second token, -4 by the twelfth, and near zero by
the fiftieth. Two adjustments fit the rest of the early signal:

- A text that begins partway through a packed row (its document id changes
  inside the row) starts weaker than the row's first text, about three
  quarters as strong.
- Within that window, function words (articles, pronouns, prepositions,
  auxiliaries) make it more negative, and tokens with no letters or digits
  (punctuation, spaces, newlines) make it less negative.

Later in a text the component is small and noisy, and this program predicts
about zero there.
"""

import math

READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    """a an the this that these those it its they them their we our us you your
    he she his her him i me my to of in on at by for with from into about as
    than and or but if so because while which who whom whose what when where
    why how is are was were be been being am do does did have has had will
    would can could shall should may might must not no there here all any
    some each every both more most other such only also just very""".split()
)

FIRST_AMPLITUDE = 12.0  # activation on the second token of the row's first text
FIRST_DECAY = 11.0  # tokens over which it fades
MID_AMPLITUDE = 9.0  # the same for a text that starts partway into the row
MID_DECAY = 10.0
FUNCTION_BOOST = 0.3  # extra negativity on function words
SYMBOL_DAMP = 0.2  # less negativity on tokens with no letters or digits


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, position in that text, whether it is the row's first text)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None:
        pos, first = 0, True
    elif doc != carry[0]:
        pos, first = 0, False
    else:
        pos, first = carry[1] + 1, carry[2]
    if pos == 0:
        return (doc, pos, first), 0.0
    if first:
        amp, decay = FIRST_AMPLITUDE, FIRST_DECAY
    else:
        amp, decay = MID_AMPLITUDE, MID_DECAY
    value = -amp * math.exp(-(pos - 1) / decay)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token.strip().lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value *= 1 + FUNCTION_BOOST
    elif not any(c.isalnum() for c in token):
        value *= 1 - SYMBOL_DAMP
    return (doc, pos, first), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3399: chat and tool-markup boundaries.

What it does, in plain terms:
- On the newline token ("\n\n") that comes right after a "<think>" or "</think>"
  tag, it writes a strong positive value (about +5): this is where the chat
  template opens or closes the reasoning block.
- On the markup tokens that end a turn or a tool message ("<|im_end|>",
  "<|endoftext|>", the word "assistant" (almost always the role name after
  "<|im_start|>"), and the tool tags "<tool_call>", "</tool_call>",
  "<tool_response>", "</tool_response>"), it writes a negative value (about -1.1).
- Everywhere else it predicts 0. The component also has a large, diffuse
  background (std about 0.85 over all tokens) that this program does not model:
  no token class, position or previous token explains it well.

These markers are the only positions where the component is reliably large and
predictable, and they are where its causal importance is concentrated.
"""

READS = ()

REASONING_TAGS = {"<think>", "</think>"}
TURN_AND_TOOL_MARKERS = {
    "<|im_end|>",
    "<|endoftext|>",
    "assistant",
    "<tool_call>",
    "</tool_call>",
    "<tool_response>",
    "</tool_response>",
}
NEWLINE_AFTER_TAG = 5.0
MARKER_VALUE = -1.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.position > 0 and token == "\n\n" and prefix.token_strings[-2] in REASONING_TAGS:
        return carry, NEWLINE_AFTER_TAG
    if token in TURN_AND_TOOL_MARKERS:
        return carry, MARKER_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3400: a near-inactive, diffuse readout.

What it is: a rank-one piece of the MLP output projection that reads mostly one
hidden unit of layer 15's MLP (hidden unit 3400, about 27% of its read vector)
and writes a fixed direction into the residual stream. Its activation is a
noisy, context-dependent number with mean about 0.025 and std about 0.29.

What I could find: no token identity, token class (letters, digits,
punctuation, spaces, newlines, CJK), previous token or position explains it
out of sample (R^2 about 0). Hidden unit 3400 itself fires on varied, unrelated
contexts (quotes, "Next" in UI instructions, "that", "um"), so it has no
readable concept either. Its causal importance is essentially zero everywhere.

So this program predicts the component's typical value everywhere. Switching
the component off barely changes the model, so this constant is the honest
description of it.
"""

READS = ()

# The component's mean activation over training text.
TYPICAL_VALUE = 0.025


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, TYPICAL_VALUE

"""Academic-citation cues for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3401.

This component is mostly quiet (about -0.1) but goes strongly negative where a
scientific or legal text writes a source reference: numbered brackets such as
"[12]" (strongest on the first digit), the "al" of "et al.", and the words that
introduce a source ("said", "according", "Fig", "Ref"). It is weaker inside
author-year parentheses such as "(Smith, 2015)". Otherwise it sits near its
baseline. The program reads only the tokens so far and scores these cues.
"""
import re

READS = ()

DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")
ATTRIBUTION = {"said", "according", "Fig", "Figure", "Ref"}

BASELINE = -0.12      # typical value away from any cue
BRACKET_OPEN = -1.4   # a "[" or ".[" that opens a bracketed reference
FIRST_NUMBER = -2.8   # first digit inside that bracket
LATER_NUMBER = -1.5   # later digits or commas inside it
ET_AL = -7.3          # "al" right after "et"
ET = -1.3             # "et"
ATTRIBUTION_WORD = -1.5
PAREN_OPEN = -0.25    # a "(" opening a parenthesis
PAREN_DIGIT = -0.6    # a digit inside a parenthesis (e.g. a year)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = s.strip()
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, None, False, "")
    _, bracket_at, in_paren, prev = carry
    i = prefix.position
    is_digit = bool(DIGIT.fullmatch(t))
    v = BASELINE
    if bracket_at is not None and i - bracket_at <= 12 and is_digit:
        v += FIRST_NUMBER if prev.endswith("[") else LATER_NUMBER
    if s.endswith("["):
        v += BRACKET_OPEN
        bracket_at = i
    elif "[" in s:
        bracket_at = i
    if "]" in s:
        bracket_at = None
    if t == "al" and prev == "et":
        v += ET_AL
    elif t == "et":
        v += ET
    if t in ATTRIBUTION:
        v += ATTRIBUTION_WORD
    if "(" in s:
        v += PAREN_OPEN
        in_paren = True
    if ")" in s:
        in_paren = False
    if in_paren and is_digit:
        v += PAREN_DIGIT
    return (doc, bracket_at, in_paren, t), v

"""Colon detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj, component 3402 (layer 15).

What it does, in plain terms: this component responds to the colon that
introduces a label, a message or a value, such as "OBSERVATION:",
"DeprecationWarning:", "Test Suites:", "Subject:", or the '":' that closes a
JSON key. Those tokens get an activation of about +2. A colon right after a
number (a time like 11:00, a ratio like 3:4) is a weaker case and gets +1.3.
Every other token gets 0.

What the simple version gets: colon-like tokens are its strongest response
(about 64% of its activations above 2.5 are colon-like), and on the eval rows
the program explains about 11% of the activation variance (Pearson r about
0.33) and about 83% of the effect of switching the component off on the
model's next-token predictions. What it leaves out: the many small,
context-dependent swings on ordinary tokens (about 90% of the variance), which
no token table, previous-token table or distance-to-colon rule explained on
held-out data.
"""

from types import SimpleNamespace

READS = ()

COLON_VALUE = 2.0  # label or message colon
NUMBER_COLON_VALUE = 1.3  # colon right after a digit: times, ratios


def is_colon(tok):
    """True for an ASCII colon, a fullwidth colon, or a token that contains one."""
    return ":" in tok or "：" in tok


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if not is_colon(tok):
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if before[-1:].isdigit():
        return carry, NUMBER_COLON_VALUE
    return carry, COLON_VALUE


def main():
    # Demo: run step over a short text, one token at a time, and print each prediction.
    text = 'OBSERVATION:\nnode:internal at 11:00, ratio 3:4, "name": "x"'
    pieces = ["OBSERVATION", ":\n", "node", ":", "internal", " at", " 11", ":", "00",
              ",", " ratio", " 3", ":", "4", ",", ' "name"', ":", ' "x"']
    assert "".join(pieces) == text
    prefix = SimpleNamespace(token_strings=[])
    carry = None
    for piece in pieces:
        prefix.token_strings.append(piece)
        carry, value = step(carry, prefix, {})
        print(f"{piece!r:14} {value:4.1f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Algebra-vocabulary detector for component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3403.

The component sits near zero on most tokens, and its clearest behaviour is a negative
response on words for mathematical equations and the algebra around them. It is most
negative on "equation" itself (about -11 on average, down to -28), and the response
weakens through three tiers of vocabulary:

- strong (about -9 to -11): "equation(s)", "inequality";
- middle (about -2 to -7): "formula", "Eq", "recurrence", "relation", "integral", "equals",
  "expression", "quadratic", "theorem", "numerator", "polynomial", "term(s)";
- weak (about -1 to -2): "equal", "identity", "linear", "sum", "condition", "constraint",
  "denominator", "solve", "fraction", "derivative", "rule", "law", "algebra".

Every other token gets 0. The program reads only the current token, so it is a word table,
not a model of context. Its variance explained is small (about 0.07): most of the
component's variance is diffuse, spread over common tokens at about 0.7 in size.
"""

READS = ()

TIERS = [
    (-10.0, ["equation", "equations", "inequality"]),
    (-5.0, ["formula", "formulas", "eq", "recurrence", "relation", "integral", "equals",
            "expression", "expressions", "quadratic", "theorem", "numerator", "polynomial"]),
    (-1.5, ["term", "terms", "equal", "identity", "linear", "sum", "condition", "constraint",
            "denominator", "solve", "fraction", "derivative", "rule", "law", "algebra"]),
]
VALUE = {word: value for value, words in TIERS for word in words}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The current token, lower-cased with its leading space removed.
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, float(VALUE.get(word, 0.0))

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3404: a near-silent, context-driven signal.

What this component is: a single rank-one slice of layer 15's MLP output. Its activation
is (hidden . V_c) * ||U_c||, and that is dominated by one MLP hidden unit, neuron 3404
(about 41% of the variance, with weight about 0.27), plus a diffuse sum over thousands of
other hidden units. Its contribution is about 0.5% of the MLP's output RMS, and it never
passes the causal-importance threshold (0 of 10M tokens).

What was checked, and what did not work:
  * It does not depend on the current token: per-token means predict nothing on held-out text.
  * It does not depend on simple token classes (digit, CJK, punctuation, leading space)
    or on the previous token's class, or on position in the document.
  * Its magnitude weakly tracks the MLP hidden norm, but its sign does not follow any
    concept we could name.
  * Its top and bottom contexts show no shared word, script or syntactic role.

So the honest program predicts the component's mean activation everywhere. It explains
essentially none of the variance, and switching it off costs almost nothing in the model.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.01  # measured mean is about 0.01 on training and eval rows


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3405 (hidden unit 3405 of that MLP).

What it does, in words: this component fires on the "own" family of words, and
most strongly on possessives that are about to be followed by "own" in a phrase like
"add your own", "create my own", "their own". It fires more weakly on the verbs of
making, adding, editing and modifying ("make", "add", "edit", "modified", "version"),
and faintly on possessive pronouns elsewhere. Its output direction promotes the next
tokens "own", "additional", "extra", "custom", "modified", so it is a "one's own /
add-on comes next" signal.

Honest scope: those word and context rules capture only a small share of the
activation's variance. Most of the activation is a diffuse background of about
+/-0.5 at ordinary tokens, which no word or short-context rule predicts.

Values are in the component's own activation units, with 0.03 the typical background.
"""

READS = ()

OWN_WORDS = {"own", "ours", "yours", "mine", "yourself", "myself", "ourselves", "custom", "customized"}
MAKE_WORDS = {
    "make", "makes", "making", "made", "add", "adds", "adding", "added",
    "edit", "edited", "modify", "modified", "modification", "modifications",
    "alter", "altered", "replace", "replaced", "create", "created", "customize",
    "adapt", "adapted", "change", "changed", "version", "fix",
}
POSSESSIVE_WORDS = {"your", "my", "our", "their", "his", "its", "her"}

BACKGROUND = 0.03
OWN_AFTER_POSSESSIVE = 1.8  # "your own", "my own", "their own"
OWN_OTHER = 0.6
POSSESSIVE_AFTER_MAKING = 0.7  # "add your", "create my", within 3 tokens of a making verb
MAKE_VERB = 0.35
POSSESSIVE_OTHER = 0.09


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids

    def back(k):
        # the word k tokens before this one, or "" if it is outside this document
        i = len(doc) - 1 - k
        if i < 0 or doc[i] != doc[-1]:
            return ""
        return prefix.token_strings[i].strip().lower()

    if word in OWN_WORDS:
        value = OWN_AFTER_POSSESSIVE if back(1) in POSSESSIVE_WORDS else OWN_OTHER
    elif word in POSSESSIVE_WORDS:
        recent = {back(1), back(2), back(3)}
        value = POSSESSIVE_AFTER_MAKING if recent & MAKE_WORDS else POSSESSIVE_OTHER
    elif word in MAKE_WORDS:
        value = MAKE_VERB
    else:
        value = BACKGROUND
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3406 (component 3406 of down_proj), read as a
"physical movement and bodily action" detector with negative sign.

The component writes its activation along a direction that suppresses
gesture/motion words in the next-token distribution. So it goes negative
while the text is describing a body or object being moved, pushed, pulled,
squeezed, shaken or otherwise physically handled, and near zero or slightly
positive elsewhere.

This program approximates it with word lists for those concepts. The current
word adds a fixed amount; a decaying running total of recent hits adds more
while a physical passage is under way. Everything else predicts 0.
"""

MOTION = set("""move moves moved moving movement movements motion motions
push pushes pushed pushing pull pulls pulled pulling press pressed pressing
squeeze squeezed squeezing thrust thrusting swing swung swinging shake shook
shaking rotate rotated rotating turn turned turning twist twisted lean leaned
leaning bend bent bending lift lifted kick kicked touch touched grab grabbed
grip hit strike tap stroke rub walk walking walked run jump roll sway wave nod
""".split())
BODY = set("""hand hands arm arms leg legs hip hips body face eyes eye head finger
fingers elbow elbows mouth feet foot shoulder chest""".split())
EXPRESSION = set("""voice breath breathing breathe smile sigh cough sniff
whisper speech speak talk talking expression facial""".split())
MANNER = set("gently gentle gentler slowly softly lightly slightly carefully".split())
FORCE = set("speed velocity acceleration force weight position direction pressure".split())
DEVICE = set("mouse click button keyboard ball".split())

WEIGHT = {}
for group, w in [(MOTION, 1.0), (EXPRESSION, 1.0), (MANNER, 1.0),
                 (BODY, 0.6), (FORCE, 0.6), (DEVICE, 0.5)]:
    for word in group:
        WEIGHT[word] = max(w, WEIGHT.get(word, 0.0))

DECAY = 0.9  # how slowly a physical passage fades
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    ema = 0.0 if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    hit = WEIGHT.get(word, 0.0)
    value = -(hit + 0.3 * ema)
    return DECAY * ema + hit, value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3407 (read through down_proj component 3407).

What it does: this component is, in effect, one hidden unit of layer 15's MLP. Its
activation is a small, noisy, mostly negative number with no simple trigger. Looking at
the token it sits on, the tokens before it, the next token, character classes and
repetition, nothing predicts it beyond about 2-4% of its variance, so this program does
not try to explain the unit's moment-to-moment values. It only encodes the two stable
facts found:
  * at a document's first token the unit is silent (about 0);
  * over the next few tokens it runs a little lower than elsewhere (about -0.08 at
    positions 1-3 of a document), and elsewhere it sits near its mean (about -0.04).

The unit's contribution to the residual stream is tiny (its RMS is about 0.4% of the
site's output), and switching it off changes the model's next-token predictions by almost
nothing, so these constants are a faithful stand-in for it.
"""

READS = ()

START = 0.0  # a document's first token

Almost nothing simple explains this component. Its activation is small and signed on
ordinary text, and its sign depends on context in a way no token list, bigram, document
or position feature captures. The one clear pattern is lexical: it is strongly negative

modal or infinitive marker ("must be", "need to", "have to", "should", "will", "can").

So the program predicts a fixed negative value on those verbs, a weaker one on the word
after a modal, and 0 everywhere else. It ignores the diffuse positive values, which carry
most of the variance, so it explains under 1% of the activation's variance on eval.

READS = ()

MODALS = {"must", "need", "needs", "should", "will", "can", "would", "could",

    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]

"""Layer 15 MLP output, component 3409: a "both / mix / choice" detector.

What it does
------------
When this component's activation is negative, its output pushes the next-token
prediction toward words of blending or choosing between options: " both", " mixed",
" either", " neither", " depending", " hybrid", " balance". Its activation is most
negative where the text is setting up such a choice or blend: "the best [of] both
worlds", "a combination [of] both", "a mix [of]", "somewhere in [between]", "it
[depends] on", "a perfect [compromise]".

This program writes that down as a rule. A word from the mix/choice list gets
-0.5. The few tokens after such a word (up to 8, in the same document) get -0.15,
so the "of" or "on" that follows "best" or "depends" also counts. Everything else
gets 0.

Honest limit: the rule captures the strongest, most readable events, but it explains
almost none of the component's variance. Most of its activation is small (typical
size 0.3) and diffuse across all token kinds, and no lookup on words or bigrams
explains much of it either (a per-token table explains about 2%). So this is a
description of what the component responds to, not a good numerical predictor.
"""

READS = ()

MIX_WORDS = frozenset(
    "both either neither depends depend depending mixed mix mixture combination "
    "balance balanced hybrid compromise between dual blend".split()
)
STRONG = -0.5  # the mix/choice word itself
WEAK = -0.15  # the next few tokens after one
WINDOW = 8  # how many tokens after a mix/choice word still count


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    # carry: (document id, tokens since the last mix/choice word)
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        since = WINDOW + 1
    else:
        since = carry[1]
    if word in MIX_WORDS:
        return (doc, 0), STRONG
    since += 1
    value = WEAK if since <= WINDOW else 0.0
    return (doc, since), value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3410 (the component's main unit), read as a mass-noun detector.

What it does: the component's activation is positive on nouns for substances,
foods, energy, and topic or field nouns (sugar, coffee, oil, health, energy, water,
security, -ics and -ology fields), most of all after "of" ("lack of electricity").
It is negative on countable, generic nouns (instance, arguments, exit, period,
method, group, team), on pronouns (it, them), on verbs and adverbs (-ed, -ly), and
slightly on digits and punctuation. Other tokens sit near zero.

The program scores each token from its own text and the token before it. Its
weights are fitted by least squares on about 3 million training positions. It is
a small, conceptual approximation: it captures the broad sign pattern, not most of
the variance, which depends on context in ways a word list cannot express.
"""

import regex
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Uncountable nouns: substances, foods, fuels, energy, and abstract mass nouns.
MASS_NOUNS = frozenset(
    """water energy food gas oil heat pressure light power air money music health
    security sugar milk rice wine coffee tea bread meat butter cream steel wood
    paper cotton gold iron glass sand soil dust smoke snow rain ice fire weather
    traffic software hardware furniture equipment advice knowledge research news
    evidence history fuel fat alcohol salt protein moisture fiber nutrition oxygen
    carbon hydrogen electricity sound noise magnetism momentum temperature humidity
    pain tax taxes insurance trade sports football guitar art beer juice soup""".split()
)

# Countable, generic nouns: slots, groups, roles, and programming terms.
COUNT_NOUNS = frozenset(
    """instance arguments exit period method group team person control point value
    code number system organization entity position command function variable class
    object option parameter argument item element step case type list file""".split()
)

PRONOUNS = frozenset("it them they he she him her us we me you its their".split())

# Endings of field and topic nouns (physics, sociology, economics, security, ...).
TOPIC_ENDINGS = ("ics", "ology", "ogy", "ism", "ist", "ity", "ness")


def _word(text):
    """The token's text if it is a whole word (letters only, at least two), else None."""
    w = text.strip()
    return w.lower() if regex.fullmatch(r"\p{L}{2,}", w) else None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = _word(text)
    if word is None:
        # Digits and punctuation sit slightly below zero.
        value = -0.2 if regex.search(r"\d", text) else -0.1 if text.strip() else 0.0
        return carry, value

    # Only look at the previous token if it belongs to the same document.
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if same_doc else ""

    value = 0.0
    is_noun = bool(wordnet.categories(word, "noun"))
    if is_noun:
        value += 0.15  # any noun sense
    elif wordnet.categories(word, "verb"):
        value -= 0.1  # verb-only words
    if prev == "of" and is_noun:
        value += 0.25  # "lack of electricity", "amount of water"
    if word in MASS_NOUNS:
        value += 1.7
        if prev == "of":
            value += 0.9
    if word in COUNT_NOUNS:
        value -= 0.7
    if word in PRONOUNS:
        value -= 0.4
    if word.endswith(TOPIC_ENDINGS):
        value += 0.85
    if word.endswith(("ed", "ly")):
        value -= 0.2
    return carry, value

The component goes negative on determiners: demonstratives and quantifiers such as this,
these, such, each, every, some, any, all, many, same, certain, and their equivalents in other
languages (diese, cette, esta, questo, данный, 该, この, ...). The strongest negatives come when
such a word opens a noun phrase right after a preposition or subordinator ("in this",
"for each", "when some"). Weaker determiners (one, other, both, few, that) and the articles
a, an, the are only slightly negative. Everything else predicts 0, and so does the first
token of a document.
"""
READS = ()

# Strongly negative: demonstratives and "each/every"-type quantifiers, mostly non-English ones.
STRONG = set(
    """each every certain various particular same such these this those
    este esta estos estas cada cualquier cette ces chaque toute toutes tous
    diese dieser dieses diesem jeder jede alle einige solche questo questa questi queste ogni
    tutti alcuni этот эта данный данном каждый любой такой различных многие некоторые
    该 这个 这些 各 每 某 同一 この その هذه هذа""".split()
)
# Moderately negative: other quantifiers.
MEDIUM = set("some any several many most all".split())
# Weakly negative: determiners and pronoun-like words that are often not attributive.
WEAK = set("one other another both few different that todo todos".split())
ARTICLES = {"a": 0.5, "an": 0.5, "the": 0.2}

# Prepositions and subordinating/coordinating words: a determiner after one is more negative.
OPENERS = set(
    """in on at for of to by with from into about through during under over after before
    between across within without against upon like as than if when whether which where while
    because since unless until and or but so how what""".split()
)


def _word(token_string):
    return token_string.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t - 1] != prefix.document_ids[t]:
        return carry, 0.0  # first token of a document has nothing before it
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[t])
    if word in STRONG:
        strength = 3.0
    elif word in MEDIUM:
        strength = 2.0
    elif word in WEAK:
        strength = 0.8
    elif word in ARTICLES:
        strength = ARTICLES[word]
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    if _word(prefix.token_strings[t - 1]) in OPENERS:
        strength *= 1.5
    return carry, -strength

The component is this unit's hidden value (its input vector puts weight 0.82 on the unit).
Its value is weakly and diffusely driven. It averages about 0.05, is near zero at a
document's first token, and the identity of the word at the position explains about 1% of
its variance. The clearest signal is at document level: a personal, review-like voice
(many I / my / we / us so far in the document) tends to push it negative, while plain
expository or narrative text sits slightly above zero.

The program predicts a baseline of 0.07 that drops with the running share of first-person
words in the current document, smoothed toward zero by a prior of 20 tokens. This explains
well under 1% of its variance; most of what the unit does is not captured by any short rule.
"""

READS = ()

FIRST_PERSON = {"i", "my", "me", "we", "our", "us"}
BASELINE = 0.07
SLOPE = 3.2
PRIOR = 20


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    count, total = (0, 0) if new_document else carry
    share = count / (total + PRIOR)
    value = BASELINE - SLOPE * share
    return (count + (word in FIRST_PERSON), total + 1), value

"""Speech openers: a negative response to exclamations, greetings and acknowledgements.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3413 is a single MLP hidden unit of
layer 15 (its input direction is almost entirely that unit), scaled by how far its write
moves the residual stream. Its activation is near zero for most text, but goes strongly
negative in casual, conversational writing, on the punctuation that directly follows a
one-word reply opener or a name/title of address:

    "Perfect!"  "Excellent!"  "Good!"  "Hello!"   -> the "!" is about -20 to -30
    "Okay,"  "Yes,"  "Sure,"  "Oh,"  "Hi Max,"      -> the "," is about -7 to -15
    "Okay" "Hi" "Thanks" (opening a sentence)       -> the word itself is about -1 to -3

Mild further negativity comes from the density of conversational markers (I, you, me, !, ?,
quote marks) in the preceding ~24 tokens, applied to commas and periods. Everything else
predicts 0. The values are rounded group means measured on training rows.

This explains only a small share of the variance: most of the component's large
activations sit in dialogue contexts that no short word list captures.
"""

READS = ()

# one-word acknowledgements, greetings and interjections that open a reply
OPENERS = {
    "perfect", "excellent", "good", "great", "hello", "hi", "hey", "okay", "ok", "alright",
    "sure", "yes", "yeah", "yep", "no", "nah", "oh", "ah", "well", "wow", "hmm", "sorry",
    "thanks", "thank",
}
# forms of address, often followed by a comma in speech
ADDRESS = {"mr", "mrs", "ms", "dr", "sir", "madam", "miss", "president", "dear"}
# conversational markers for the register density term
MARKERS = {"i", "you", "me", "my", "your", "we", "!", "?", '"', "“", "”"}
PUNCT = {",", "!", "?", ".", "...", "，", "！", "？", "。"}


def word(text):
    """A token's bare lowercase word, without spaces or punctuation."""
    return text.strip().strip(".,!?;:\"'“”‘’…-").lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    # the first token of a document has no earlier token to react to
    if len(tokens) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    cur, prev = tokens[-1].strip(), tokens[-2].strip()

    # "!" right after a reply opener or a form of address: the strongest response
    if cur in ("!", "！") and word(prev) in OPENERS | ADDRESS:
        return None, -20.0
    # "!" right after any capitalized word
    if cur in ("!", "！") and prev[:1].isupper():
        return None, -13.0
    # "," right after a reply opener or a form of address
    if cur in (",", "，") and word(prev) in OPENERS | ADDRESS:
        return None, -7.0
    # other punctuation right after a reply opener
    if cur in PUNCT and word(prev) in OPENERS:
        return None, -1.7
    # the opener word itself, when it is the current token
    if word(tokens[-1]) in OPENERS:
        return None, -2.0 if tokens[-1][:1].isupper() else -1.0
    # commas and periods in conversational text: more negative the more markers nearby
    if cur in (",", "，", "."):
        window = [t.strip().lower() for t in tokens[-25:-1]]
        density = sum(1 for t in window if word(t) in MARKERS or t in MARKERS) / 24
        return None, -6.0 * density
    return None, 0.0

readable token-level pattern. The best simple thing we found is a sign by
character class of the current token: word tokens that begin with a space lean

    if s[0] in SENT_PUNCT:

    return "other"

    "math_op": 0.016,
    "sent_punct": -0.030,
    "nonascii": 0.012,
    "other": 0.002,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    value = CLASS_MEAN[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])]
    return carry, value

activation is a dense, context-dependent signal. Its value is not a function of
the current token (a per-token lookup explains ~1% of its variance), of the next
token (an oracle lookup explains none), or of any simple surface feature of the

the first tokens of a document sit a little above the unit's typical value,
and from about the 16th token on it sits at its typical value, about -0.05.

document, using bucket means measured on training rows. It carries no other
information, and it explains very little variance: the honest summary is that

token's position in it.

    (0, -0.006),   # first token of a document
    (1, 0.060),    # second token
    (2, 0.040),    # tokens 3 to 8
    (8, 0.003),    # tokens 9 to 16
    (16, -0.050),  # everything later: the unit's typical value
]

    value = BUCKETS[0][1]
    for start, mean in BUCKETS:

    return value

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    return (doc, pos), _bucket(pos)

this program predicts only the broad trend: a digit that follows a dense run of digits
gets a high value, a digit in a looser run gets a middling value, and all other tokens

(within the same document) are single digits.

(about 1.0 and 0.3) because held-out samples disagree on the best scale.

variance (chunk-level R^2 of about 0.007 on average, sometimes negative). The rest is

    """Activation at the newest token, from its word class."""
    return carry, VALUE.get(word_class(prefix.token_strings[-1]), BASE)

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's down_proj whose input direction is
dominated by MLP hidden unit 3445 (0.76 of its unit norm, 58% of its squared norm; the rest is

It is a dense, sign-varying signal: std 0.74, both signs, large values on about 1% of tokens.

- the token identity (per-token mean, shrunk): held-out R^2 about 0.04 at best, and
  about 0 for plain per-token means;
- the previous token, bigrams and tokens 2 to 8 back: R^2 at most about 0.016;
- position in the document, distance since a newline or period, bracket depth, quotes,
  repetition of the token earlier in the document, script and word-like categories,
  and word frequency: all within R^2 0.01 of zero;
- document-level means: R^2 about 0.02, which is mostly overfit.

So no short readable rule predicts its sign. Predicting zero scores activation variance
explained of about 0. Switching the component off changes the model's next-token predictions
by almost nothing (KL 7.6e-6 nats per position), so a zero prediction reproduces that effect.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Always predict zero: no token, position or context feature found that carries the sign."""
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3446, read through its down_proj component.

The component's activation is mostly this one MLP hidden unit (its input vector V is
dominated by coordinate 3446, and the activation correlates 0.62 with that unit's value).
That unit is silu(gate) * up: it is strongly negative only when the gate is open and the
up projection is strongly negative. The result is rare bursts: about 0.1% of tokens fall
below -3, and the largest reach -30. Its output direction, when the activation is negative,
promotes words like "which one", "one of them", "whichever", "mostly", "majority".

Those bursts sit near moments where the text names or weighs a choice ("Answer:",
"Correct", "option", "choose", "decide", "go with"), but that is only a weak trigger:
most such words are not bursts, and most bursts have no such word. Surface rules
(words, scripts, token identity, position, entropy of the model's own prediction) explain
almost nothing.

So this program is a lexical proxy: on a choice word it predicts -0.6 (roughly the mean
activation on such words in training text), and 0 everywhere else.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

CHOICE_WORDS = {
    "answer", "answers", "ans", "correct", "option", "options", "choose", "chose",
    "choice", "choices", "pick", "decide", "opt", "prefer", "vote",
}
VALUE = -0.6  # mean activation on choice words in a sample of training text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[prefix.position].strip().lower()
    return carry, (VALUE if word in CHOICE_WORDS else 0.0)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3447: a diffuse, near-constant offset.

What it does: predicts the component's typical activation, a small positive
constant (about 0.028), at every token, except that a document's first token
gets 0, since the component is essentially silent there.

Why: the component's activation is spread over a dense mix of residual-stream
directions. It has no token-identity, position, repetition, or confidence
pattern that a short program can capture (held-out checks: token identity
explains under 1% of variance, token-class and repetition features nothing).
It is almost never important to the model's output (switching it off changes
the next-token distribution by about 1e-6 nats). So the honest short
description is its mean level, not a feature it detects.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0283  # mean over eval-like rows; std is 0.27 around it


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3448 (through the component's direction) in Qwen3-1.7B.

This component reads almost one MLP hidden unit: the layer-15 MLP's hidden unit 3448,
scaled by about 1.1. Its value is noisy and depends on the wider sentence rather than on
any single word. Token identity alone explains about 1% of its variance, so no word list
gets far.

The one readable pattern found: a subject pronoun ("he", "she", "they", "it", "we", "I",
"you", "who") that directly follows a subordinating conjunction ("because", "when",
"after", "if", ...) starts a clause and tends to push the unit negative. Everywhere else
the program predicts 0, the mean of the activation.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

SUBJECT_PRONOUNS = {"he", "she", "they", "it", "we", "i", "you", "who"}
SUBORDINATORS = {
    "because", "when", "after", "if", "as", "since", "while", "although",
    "so", "where", "before", "until", "unless", "once",
}
CLAUSE_PULL = -0.43  # mean activation at such positions in the training sample


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    if word in SUBJECT_PRONOUNS and before in SUBORDINATORS:

    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 3449.

Most of this component's activation is diffuse: it has std ~0.66 over ordinary text, but no
token, token class, document or chat role predicts it (held-out R^2 ~ 0). Its causal importance is
near zero almost everywhere, so the model barely reads it there.

Where it does matter is one spot: the first newline pair after an empty reasoning block,
"</think>\\n\\n" at the start of a chat reply. There the component is strongly negative
(about -1.6 on average, from -0.2 to -3). This program predicts that spike and 0 elsewhere.
"""

READS = ()

SPIKE = -1.6  # mean activation on the "\n\n" that follows "</think>"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    hit = len(toks) >= 2 and toks[-1] == "\n\n" and toks[-2] == "</think>"
    return carry, (SPIKE if hit else 0.0)

"""Constant predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3450.

This component's activation has no simple concept behind it: it is a small,
context-dependent value with mean about -0.04 and spread about 0.33, and it
hardly depends on the current token, the previous token, the character class
or the position in the document. The only regularity found is that the first
token of each document sits at about zero. This program predicts the typical
value everywhere except that first token.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = -0.042  # mean activation over ordinary positions
FIRST_TOKEN = 0.0  # a document's first token: activation is about 0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    d = prefix.document_ids
    if len(d) == 1 or d[-1] != d[-2]:
        return carry, FIRST_TOKEN
    return carry, TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 3451: a diffuse, mostly-noise feature.

What it is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. Its activation is
(hidden . V) * |U|, and about 40% of V's weight sits on the MLP hidden unit 3451 itself,
so it is roughly that unit's output. Over a corpus its activation is near zero most of
the time (std 0.36) with occasional spikes of either sign (down to -25, up to +7).

What we could find: the activation is NOT explained by the current token's identity
(about 1% of variance), by the previous token, by the document, by the position in a
document, by repeated phrases, or by coarse character classes. The most negative
tokens are unit-of-measure words (tsp, tablespoons, grams, meters) and exam-prep
phrases, the most positive are web and code boilerplate (e.g. '/src', '@@'), but these token
classes move the prediction by far too little to show in variance explained: a unit-word
density proxy reaches R^2 of 0.0002 on training rows.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value, about -0.02,
and predicts 0 at the first token of each document (or of a row), where the component
is silent (mean -0.007, spread 0.003). Nothing else is modelled: the score is
essentially zero (eval variance explained about 0, e2e KL the same as switching it off).
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL_VALUE = -0.0217  # the component's mean activation away from document starts


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A document's first token: the row's first token, or the first token after a
    # change of document label. There the component is silent.
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    at_start = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if at_start else TYPICAL_VALUE

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3452, read as the activation of MLP hidden unit 3452 in
layer 15 (it carries about 55% of this component's variance).

Mostly it is small noise: about -0.1 on symbols and about -0.05 on plain words, with a few
large spikes. The big spikes come at one recognisable place, the opening sentence of an
encyclopaedia-style biography such as "Name (born 12 May 1950) is a ...":
  - the ')' that closes a parenthesis holding a birth or death date goes strongly negative
    (mean about -8, often -10 to -27 in the data),
  - and so does the 'is' or 'was' right after that ')'.
Weaker negative values go to the other ')' and sentence ends in that opening sentence, and to
'is' / 'was' there after the first few tokens. Nothing else is modelled.

State kept per document: sentences ended so far (0 means still in the opening sentence), the
text of the open parenthesis and whether it sits in the opening sentence, and whether the last
token closed a date parenthesis.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# A parenthesis holds a date if it says "born", or has a year, or a range of years.
DATE = re.compile(r"\b1[5-9]\d\d\b|\b20\d\d\b.*[–—-]|[–—-].*\b(1[5-9]\d\d|20\d\d)\b")
SENTENCE_END = {".", "!", "?", "。"}

DATE_CLOSE = -6.0         # ')' closing a date parenthesis in the opening sentence
COPULA_AFTER_DATE = -6.0  # 'is' / 'was' right after such a ')'
LEAD_COPULA = -1.0        # 'is' / 'was' later in the opening sentence (after 8 tokens)
LEAD_PUNCT = -0.4         # other ')' and sentence ends in the opening sentence
BASELINE = -0.12          # symbols, digits and spaces: a little below the component's mean
WORD_BASELINE = -0.05     # plain words: a little above the mean


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "n": 0, "sentences": 0, "paren": None, "lead": False, "after": False}
    lead = carry["sentences"] == 0
    value = BASELINE if not word.isalpha() else WORD_BASELINE
    if carry["after"] and word in ("is", "was"):
        value = COPULA_AFTER_DATE
    elif lead and word in ("is", "was") and carry["n"] >= 8:
        value = LEAD_COPULA
    elif lead and word in SENTENCE_END:
        value = LEAD_PUNCT
    carry["after"] = False
    if "(" in tok:
        carry["paren"] = ""
        carry["lead"] = lead
    elif carry["paren"] is not None:
        carry["paren"] += tok
    if ")" in tok and carry["paren"] is not None:
        text = carry["paren"]
        if carry["lead"] and ("born" in text or DATE.search(text)):
            value = DATE_CLOSE
            carry["after"] = True
        elif carry["lead"]:
            value = LEAD_PUNCT
        carry["paren"] = None
    if word in SENTENCE_END:
        carry["sentences"] += 1
    carry["n"] += 1
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3453 (this component's input direction is almost entirely that unit).

What it does: the unit is a weak, mostly negative signal whose size depends on how far into its
document the token sits. The first token of each document reads exactly 0. Over the next ~20
tokens it sits around -0.2 to -0.3; deep into a long document it drifts back toward -0.06.
Nothing about the current word explains the rest: token identity, the previous token, repeated
words and the document's genre each add only a little. So this program predicts the position
profile alone, and counts positions within each document (restarting where the document changes).
"""

READS = ()

# (first position in its document where the bucket starts, mean activation in the bucket)
PROFILE = [
    (1, -0.21),
    (2, -0.28),
    (3, -0.29),
    (10, -0.26),
    (20, -0.20),
    (50, -0.15),
    (100, -0.10),
    (200, -0.06),
]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label of the previous token, its position in the document)
    label = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or label != carry[0]:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    value = 0.0  # a document's first token is exactly 0
    for start, mean in PROFILE:
        if pos >= start:
            value = mean
    return (label, pos), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 3454.

It responds to indentation and to line numbers, in plain terms:
- Indentation that changes. The first run of spaces or tabs on a line is compared with the
  first run on the previous line. Deeper gives a strong response (about 6.5), shallower a
  moderate one (about 3.4), and the same gives about zero. Lines with no indentation give
  nothing.
- Line numbers. In a listing that prints a line number at the start of each line, the
  second and later digits of the number fire (about 2.6), and so does the whitespace that
  follows the number (about 3.1).
- Digits in running text: 2-9 fire a little (about 0.7), 0 and 1 weakly (about 0.2).
- Other spaces or tabs inside a line fire slightly (about 0.3).
Everything else is about zero.

This is a readable approximation. The real activation varies a lot with context these
rules do not see, so most of its variance is left unexplained.
"""

import re

READS = ()

WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"[ \t ]+")
DIGIT = re.compile(r"[0-9]")
LINE_NUMBER_SO_FAR = re.compile(r"[ \t ]*[0-9]+")

DEEPER = 6.5
SHALLOWER = 3.4
AFTER_LINE_NUMBER_DIGIT = 2.6
AFTER_LINE_NUMBER_SPACE = 3.1
INLINE_SPACE = 0.3
DIGIT_2_TO_9 = 0.7
DIGIT_0_OR_1 = 0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the document, the first indent of the previous line, and the current line's text so far
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "prev": 0, "line": ""}
    before = carry["line"]

    if "\n" in token:
        # the first token of the line that just ended becomes the previous indent
        first = carry.get("first", 0)
        carry = {"doc": doc, "prev": first, "line": token.split("\n")[-1], "first": 0}
        return carry, 0.0

    carry = {"doc": doc, "prev": carry["prev"], "line": before + token, "first": carry.get("first", 0)}
    if WHITESPACE.fullmatch(token):
        if before == "":
            n = len(token)
            carry["first"] = n
            if n > carry["prev"]:
                return carry, DEEPER
            if n < carry["prev"]:
                return carry, SHALLOWER
            return carry, 0.0
        if LINE_NUMBER_SO_FAR.fullmatch(before):
            return carry, AFTER_LINE_NUMBER_SPACE
        return carry, INLINE_SPACE
    if DIGIT.fullmatch(token):
        if LINE_NUMBER_SO_FAR.fullmatch(before):
            return carry, AFTER_LINE_NUMBER_DIGIT
        return carry, DIGIT_0_OR_1 if token in "01" else DIGIT_2_TO_9
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 3455: the "of" of quantities and parts.

What it does: it fires on the preposition that links a quantity or part noun to
the whole it belongs to: "most OF the", "a fraction OF", "the majority OF", "some
OF", "percent OF", "portion OF", and the Romance equivalents ("la mayoría DE",
"el resto DE", "un grupo DE"). Ordinary "of" after other nouns ("the number of",
"the use of") fires moderately. "of" inside fixed phrases ("instead of",
"because of", "out of", "instance of") fires weakly. Every other token is ~0,
and the first token of a document is 0.

The values are the mean activations measured on training text. The program only
reads the previous word, so it is causal.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

# The English "of" and its Romance counterparts ("de", "di", "del", "der", ...).
OF_WORDS = {"of"}
DE_WORDS = {
    "de", "di", "del", "der", "des", "von", "van", "dei", "av", "da", "dos", "della", "delle",
}

# Quantity and part nouns and quantifiers: the "of" after them is a partitive.
PARTITIVE = {
    "many", "most", "some", "majority", "rest", "each", "both", "several", "few", "none",
    "either", "any", "all", "fraction", "portion", "percent", "percentage", "proportion",
    "subset", "half", "piece", "pieces", "part", "parts", "bulk", "amount", "lot", "lots",
    "range", "remainder", "number", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "more", "much",
    "couple", "pair", "bit", "quarter", "third", "extent", "sum", "share", "total",
    "plenty", "mayoría", "mayoria", "resto", "%", "serie", "série", "partie", "parte",
    "uno", "nombre", "número", "numero", "porcentaje", "tipo", "grupo", "maioria", "helft",
}

# Fixed multi-word prepositions, whose "of" is weak.
FIXED = {
    "instead", "because", "out", "instance", "consist", "consists", "consisting",
    "comprised", "composed", "made", "terms", "case", "place", "country", "town", "city",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # The first token of each document has no context: 0.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if word in OF_WORDS:
        if prev in PARTITIVE:
            return carry, 5.3
        if prev in FIXED:
            return carry, 1.7
        return carry, 3.9
    if word in DE_WORDS:
        return carry, 3.0 if prev in PARTITIVE else 1.0
    return carry, 0.0
